newsitem.title: USA: Lebanon gets $165 million World Bank loan.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon gets $165 million World Bank loan.

text.p: The World Bank said on Tuesday that it approved $165 million in financing to help the Lebanese government complete reconstruction of its war-damaged electricity supply system.
The package includes a $65 million loan at the bank's standard variable interest rate for LIBOR-based U.S.-dollar single-currency loans. It has a grace period and maturity of nine years.

The bank said it will also provide lending and a partial credit guarantee for the principal of a $100-million bond Eurobond issue by the Republic of Lebanon, with a tranche placed in the United States -- the first ever such placement by Lebanon.

The guarantee will lengthen maturity for the issue to 10 years, compared with previous Lebanese government bond issues with three- to five-year maturities. It will also reduce spreads by a factor of three to about 100 basis points.
The guarantee is also intended to broaden the investor base to include international institutional investors.
